pages.title: Amber Nautilus
pages.text:
Concentric rings of amber and teal spiral inward toward a luminous cyan vortex, the whole figure turning like a chambered shell cut in half. The square-dither perturbation roughens the ring edges into beaded chains, and the zzold feedback transform layers each step’s history into the next. The centroid-distance metric colors each solve by how far its root cloud center sits from the origin — the outermost rings are farthest, glowing gold; the inner spiral is closest, shining cyan. The reef palette completes the oceanic illusion.

pages.title: Crown of Thorns
pages.text:
A single rust-and-ember crown floats in a vast field of concentric brown ripples, its circumference dotted with small dark voids like thorns worked into the metal. Seventy roots per solve sweep around the unit circle through the swirler coefficient transform and reversal — the swirler twists the coefficient vector like taffy before the reversal folds it back on itself. The clusteriness score at a tight 1.5 percent clip lights up where the nearest neighbors pack most densely, and the desert-warmwhite-ember tri-palette paints the crown in ember and the surrounding rings in burnt umber. The dark perforations are the solve points where no root cluster ever forms, small holes burned into the metal band.

pages.title: Magenta Galaxy
pages.text:
A swirling galactic vortex of magenta and silver dust spirals around a hollow violet core, rendered from the same p11b3 polynomial family that produced earlier passes from this compute job. Ten roots per solve are pushed through the roots5 parameter transform — a fifth-root lattice that fractures the smooth coefficient sweep into discrete spiral arms — and an autolevels pass pulls every filament out of the shadows. The composition reads as a long-exposure photograph of a slowly rotating galactic disc: dark hollow core, dense inner spiral, faint silver outer arms dissolving into the void.

p11b3 · degree 10 · 5000×5000 · autolevels

pages.title: Spectrum Eye
pages.text:
A luminous iris layered with concentric rainbow rings — orange core, yellow pupil, green pupil-ring, indigo inner shell, green mid-ring, blue outer shell — bristled with fine radial spikes at the perimeter. Seventy roots per solve from the creative10 function are pushed through the zzold parameter transform that feeds each step's output back as the next step's input, then resolved by the companion-matrix eigensolver so every eigenvalue lands exactly. The nearest-neighbor variation score at a five percent clip lights up where each root's closest sibling keeps changing identity, and the turbo palette wraps the full visible spectrum around the density gradient. The result reads as a cosmic eye seen through a prism, every ring a separate frequency of the same underlying root cloud. This is a resized print of an autolevels original.

pages.title: Rust Iris
pages.text:
A turquoise aperture rings a cloud of rust and amber dust, the whole figure suspended on a faint halo of concentric ripples. The creative9 coefficient function with an eleven-parameter vector is pushed through a zero-one parameter warp and a sixth-coefficient twist, then the coefficients are run through a sort-cumulative-sum scramble that layers the orderings on top of each other. The outlierness score at a five-percent clip lights up the roots that stray farthest from the median radial distance, and the reef palette frames the burning interior with a cool teal eye-ring. At the center a dark pupil opens onto the void where all ten roots cluster near coincidence.

pages.title: Aureate Egg
pages.text:
A luminous torus of teal and gold cradles a braided interior of amber curtains and folded coefficient-space geometry — a cosmic egg with its shell peeled back to reveal the nested spirals inside. Thirty-four roots per solve are pushed through the unit-circle parameter sweep and a second-coefficient transform, then reversed at the coefficient stage. The outlierness score at a five-percent clip picks out the roots that wander farthest from the median radial distance, and the reef palette flares cyan where the shell thins and amber where it thickens. Above the egg, faint spines radiate outward — the signature of roots that briefly escaped before the solver caught them and pulled them back.

pages.title: Cerulean Owl
pages.text:
The same apparition returns: a pale blue face with horned crests and hollow eyes, now rendered in the stark blue-white-red palette instead of a rainbow index. Thirty-five roots per solve sweep around the unit circle through a second-coefficient warp, then reverse at the coefficient stage to enforce the bilateral symmetry. The outlierness score at a five-percent clip picks out the structural outliers — the roots that drift farthest from their siblings' median radius — and the bwred palette stains the horned silhouette in icy blue with flashes of coral where the shell ruptures. Same uncanny portrait as Spectral Owl, painted in a cooler hand.

pages.title: Triquetra
pages.text:
Three translucent teal circles overlap in a perfect trefoil, their intersections darkening to indigo, with a small amber sun burning at the geometric center. Thirty-four roots per solve are swept around the unit circle through a seventh-coefficient transform, then reversed — a structural recipe that locks in the three-lobed rotational symmetry. The shelliness score measures how uniformly roots distribute around their centroid, and the reef palette paints the uniform shells in cool cyan and the amber pistil where the shell collapses to a point. A wide twenty-times square extent pulls the full orbital structure into view. The effect is a Celtic knot rendered from root orbits.

pages.title: Infinity Links
pages.text:
Two interlocked horizontal ovals in teal and amber glide across a black field like a pair of chained links or an infinity sign cast in liquid metal. Eight roots per solve — low enough that each carves a distinct surface — are swept around the unit circle and reversed at the coefficient stage, producing the mirror symmetry. The proximity score at a tight 0.1% clip with omega enabled lights up where the nearest pair of roots comes closest to collision, and the reef palette traces the collision seams in cyan and the relaxed arcs in amber. The dark hollows inside the rings are the structural voids where no root cluster ever forms, fixed points in the parameter sweep.

pages.title: Prismatic Moth
pages.text:
Two broad iridescent wings banded with the full visible spectrum float diagonally across a black field, flanking a compact rainbow thorax cluster. Nine roots per solve — low enough that each moves independently with room to breathe — are swept through the unit circle and a third-coefficient transform, then reversed. The proximity score at a tight 0.1% clip with omega enabled lights up the tightest near-collisions, and the rainbow_d3 palette wraps D3's smooth rainbow gradient around the density gradient. The moth form arrives by accident: the giga_53 function just happens to produce this diagonal bilateral creature, and the nine-root degree gives each wing band its own distinct hue.

The outlierness score lights up roots straying farthest from the median radial distance at a five-percent clip, and the inferno palette paints the dense interior in dark plum and the outlier quills in burning gold. The result is a microbial portrait — sea urchin, virus, or seed pod, depending on how you read the geometry.

Where the shell is even, the color is dark; where roots bunch along one radius, the red-gold palette flares to life at the blade tips.

A ring of crimson embers surrounds a dark cavity, with pale ash-gray shards radiating outward. The nn-variation score measures how inconsistently each root's nearest neighbor changes across the parameter space — high variation means the neighborhood is unstable, and those zones glow brightest.

The shelliness score colors the image by radial uniformity — where roots form a neat shell around the centroid the tone is flat; where they clump along one axis, the warm palette intensifies. The result is an accidental totem, its expression shifting with each slight change in the coefficient function.

The disk-dither perturbation softens the geometry, and the low grid count leaves each bead individually resolved, each one a miniature solve where the root cluster pattern differs subtly from its neighbors.

At degree seventy, the roots compress into a gilded sphere ribbed with fine radial teeth, split by a violet meridian where conjugate symmetry breaks. Filaments of scattered light radiate outward — the outliers, roots that escaped the gravitational center, glowing brightest in the inferno palette where deviation from the median is greatest.

pages.title: Basketwork Moon

The centroid-distance metric measures how far each solve's root cloud centroid drifts from the origin, with omega=6 periodic remapping producing the multiple concentric shells. pages.title: Gilded Coil
pages.text:

Forty-nine roots per solve from the moth4 function are pushed through the xim parameter transform and reversed at the coefficient stage. The anisotropy score at a five percent clip lights up where the local root cloud stretches asymmetrically — where the roots stop distributing isotropically and start elongating along one axis — and the ink-gold-lavender tri-palette stains the stretched zones in gold and the relaxed zones in soft lavender. The gap in the ring is where the anisotropy breaks down entirely, the filaments dissolving into the small detached cluster that hangs outside the main loop.

The square-dither perturbation scatters the parameter grid just enough to roughen every surface, and the zzold transform folds old coefficient history back into the current step. The outlierness score picks out roots that stray farthest from the median radial distance — the cyan shards are the structural outliers, glowing where the annulus erodes. pages.title: Golden Archipelago
pages.text:
A sprawling golden landmass with dark volcanic eyes and violet undershadows floats among a scatter of smaller islands and droplets. The polynomial alternates even and odd coefficient rules — even indices divide by the index, odd indices multiply and add a logarithmic offset — creating a root cloud that fragments into distinct territories. The crowding score measures mean pairwise log-distance, and the gilded palette maps dense crowds to burnished gold and sparse voids to deep purple. The parallel Aberth solver races through twenty-five million solves to fill every inlet.

pages.title: Frozen Dahlia
pages.text:

Forty-nine roots per solve create the petal count; the coeff5 transform and reversal enforce the rotational symmetry. The crowding score measures mean log-distance between all root pairs, and the blue-white-red palette maps that density gradient into a frozen botanical: blue where roots breathe, white where they crowd, red at the dense heart where the polynomial’s structure collapses to a singularity.

pages.title: Abyssal Iris
pages.text:
The same palindromic polynomial that produced the Cyclops Nebula, now recolored by clusteriness — how tightly nearest-neighbor roots pack. The result is an iris of deep teal and copper, its pupil ringed by a corrugated corona of densely clustered roots that glow amber in the reef palette. The surrounding haze is where roots spread thin, their spacing too wide to register on the cluster score. Fifty roots per solve, four thousand squared parameter pairs, each one a separate eigenvalue problem.

pages.title: Unit Circle Scar
pages.text:
The same polynomial again, but now the distance-from-unit-circle metric reveals a different anatomy. The bright amber ring is where roots sit closest to |z|=1, and the teal glow marks where they drift away. The dark pupil at the center is unchanged — it is the structural void where no roots land regardless of the metric. This pair of images, Abyssal Iris and Unit Circle Scar, demonstrates how the same root cloud tells completely different stories depending on which geometric property you measure.

pages.title: Beaded Eye
pages.text:
A teal iris rings a black pupil, its inner edge studded with amber beads, the whole figure suspended in a loose square cloud of cyan and copper dust with small amber spots at each corner. Twenty-five roots per solve are pushed through the swirler coefficient transform and reversed, with no parameter transform — raw grid coordinates drive the geometry directly. The nearest-neighbor variation score at a tight 1.5 percent clip lights up where each root's closest sibling keeps changing identity across the parameter sweep, and the reef palette stains the stable interior in cyan and the unstable outer dust in warm amber. The four corner spots are fixed points where specific roots lock in place regardless of where the parameters go.

pages.title: Amber Rosary
pages.text:
The same giga_25 polynomial colored by a different metric: the iris now reads as a thick amber rosary, its twenty-five beads articulated in warm gold with fine teal highlights, still suspended in the same square dust cloud. Pushed through the swirler coefficient transform and reversed without a parameter transform, the coefficient field is identical to Beaded Eye — only the coloring metric changes. The clusteriness score at a 1.5 percent clip lights up where the nearest neighbors pack most tightly, and the reef palette flares amber at those dense points. Where Beaded Eye shows neighbor instability, this image shows neighbor density; the underlying root geometry is the same cloud viewed through a different lens.

pages.title: Anemone Crown
pages.text:

The polynomial folds its ten coefficients through a cumulative sum and a reversal, then sweeps the parameters around the unit circle — a structural recipe that forces the radial symmetry. The dist-unit-circle metric scores each solve by how far its roots stray from |z|=1: warm amber where roots sit on the circle itself, cool cyan where they drift away. The reef palette gives the result its bioluminescent stillness, like deep-water life caught mid-pulse.

pages.title: Mirror Spawn

Each crescent is a ribcage of fine filaments, the vertebrae articulated by the square-dither perturbation that scatters the parameter grid into a granular cloud. Twenty-two roots per solve, swept five times across a five-thousand-square parameter mesh, produce nearly three billion individual root positions. The shelliness score measures how uniformly each root cloud distributes around its centroid, and the red-gold palette flares brightest where the shells fracture into structural disorder. The fine lattice records every orbital path the roots traced as the parameters swept around the unit circle, and the coefficient reversal locks in the bilateral symmetry.
